newsitem.title: USA: Texas wheat condition declines amid stormy weather.
newsitem.headline: Texas wheat condition declines amid stormy weather.

text.p: The condition of the Texas wheat crop declined during the week ended Sunday as violent weather hit the state, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop progress report.
A return to warmer, calmer weather by late week improved crop conditions in most areas.

Winter wheat was rated six percent very poor, 16 poor, 35 fair, 32 good and 11 excellent. A week earlier, wheat rated three percent very poor, 15 poor, 40 fair, 35 good and seven excellent. Wheat was three percent harvested, against one last week, 11 last year and eight percent on average.

Corn was 15 percent silked, against 25 percent last year and 26 on average. Fields were in the dough stage in the Rio Grande Valley, Coastal Bend and into central Texas. Corn condition was rated nil very poor, three percent poor, 25 fair, 49 good and 23 percent excellent.
Sorghum was 72 percent planted versus 74 a year ago and 80 percent on average. Sorghum was rated nil very poor, two percent poor, 18 fair, 57 good and 23 excellent.
Sunflowers were 33 percent planted versus 40 a year ago and 47 on average. Cotton was 73 percent planted, versus 55 last year and 67 on average.
